hero: At a kitchen table in a concrete farmhouse in Isabela, a Filipino nephrology fellow shows a printed chart of dialysis, transplant and conservative care to a 56-year-old Filipino woman and her husband in farm clothes, while their daughter appears on a smartphone video call propped against a water jug; rice fields visible through the open window, warm afternoon light, no text.

figures.teaches: Each kidney replacement option asks different things of the patient and family, and the choice rests on the patient's goals.
figures.content: Center circle 'What matters to the patient: work, family, home, travel, comfort'. Four surrounding panels. 'In-center hemodialysis': 'about 3 sessions a week, about 4 hours', 'travel and a companion', 'PhilHealth: up to 156 sessions a year if PDD-registered; fares not covered'. 'Peritoneal dialysis at home': 'daily exchanges or overnight machine', 'clean space, hand hygiene, helper if vision is poor', 'PhilHealth PD Z benefit'. 'Kidney transplant': 'living or deceased donor', 'lifelong medicines', 'few centers'. 'Comprehensive conservative management': 'no dialysis, active symptom care', 'advance care planning', 'valid choice (KDIGO 2024)'. Footer: 'Present all four to every patient'.

figures.teaches: Preparation for kidney replacement is triggered by risk months before the start, and the start itself is triggered by symptoms.
figures.content: Left-to-right timeline. Marker 1 'KFRE 5-year 3-5%: refer to nephrology'. Marker 2 'KFRE 2-year >10%: multidisciplinary care'. Marker 3 'KFRE 2-year >40% or eGFR below about 15-20: modality education, family meeting, protect veins, hepatitis B vaccine, transplant referral, PDD paperwork'. Marker 4 'Access placed: fistula matures or PD catheter heals'. Marker 5 'Symptoms or signs (often GFR 5-10): planned start'. Inset box: 'IDEAL, 828 adults: deaths 37.6% early vs 36.6% late start (HR 1.04); 75.9% of late group started earlier for symptoms'. All thresholds labeled 'KDIGO 2024 practice point'.

card: A farmer and his wife at a kitchen table looking at a printed chart with a young doctor, rice fields through the window, no text.
